articles.title: Alexander Volkov: 'Of course' Dana White didn't recognize me at UFC presser — 'I'm not even sure he can remember my name'
articles.summary: "I bet every time he hears my name, he thinks they're talking about Alexander Volkanovski," the Russian contender said of his viral exchange with the UFC bos...
articles.body:
Alexander Volkov remains a model of consistency within the UFC heavyweight ranks.

At UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi this past Saturday, Volkov kept his win streak alive, defeating Rizvan Kuniev by unanimous decision . The performance extended Volkov's streak of success to three straight, with only one loss coming over his past eight appearances.

Notably, Volkov, 38, made a surprise appearance at the event's pre-fight press conference to confront UFC CEO Dana White and ask what he needed to do to earn his first UFC title shot. White initially appeared not to recognize Volkov, despite the heavyweight having fought 20 times in the promotion. The scene went viral as White awkwardly went back and forth with Volkov, with featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski even trying to help White out as he sat to White's right on the stage.

On Wednesday's edition of "The Ariel Helwani Show," Volkov said he wasn't scheduled to be part of the press conference, which is how he came up with the idea of entering as a crowd member. Regarding whether White recognized him, he believes it was obvious he didn't.

"Of course he didn't recognize me," Volkov told Uncrowned. "First of all, I'm a Russian fighter. I'm not even sure he can remember my name. I bet every time he hears my name, he thinks they're talking about Alexander Volkanovski.

"It's fine. There is 500 or more fighters on the roster, so he doesn't recognize every fighter. But to talk seriously, he still didn't have an answer [to] my question. I asked him, 'What should I do? What am I supposed to do to get a title fight?' They don't have this answer every time.

"[Fighters] don't decide [who gets it]," Volkov added. "I'm just doing my job."

Nearly a week later, Volkov is still awaiting an answer, as White was non-committal about a title shot for Volkov at the post-fight press conference, despite his Kuniev victory. "Drago" admits he's feeling the love and support from fans saying he should be next, though.

Ultimately, he isn't overly upset about not getting an answer either.

"I'm never disappointed with something anymore. I'm too old for that. I just know what I should do," Volkov said.

"In the best way, I can't cry everywhere that I deserve it, or I'm next. What I can do is just ask the bosses what I'm supposed to do. This is the only question I have for them. Just give me things I should do, because I did a lot. I'm like the most proven fighter in the UFC [heavyweight division] right now. I'm on my win streak, in my prime, I can do good with everything with every fighter right now. I'm the best striker in the UFC. I have a black belt in BJJ. I can fight with anybody; it doesn't matter who is my opponent."

One of the biggest knocks on Volkov over his latest run has been his lack of finishes. Volkov hasn't knocked out or submitted an opponent since his second-round Ezekiel choke of Tai Tuivasa in September 2023.

Volkov isn't sitting back and over-inflating a narrative that he's been a wildly exciting fighter in recent fights. He sees his claim more as a testament to his strength of schedule, and if that means more competitive fights, he's fine with it.

"To be honest, I'm not kind of hunting for this title," Volkov said. "This belt doesn't define me. I'm still a champion by myself. I understand who I am, what I can do, which guys I can beat. It's opposite. Fighter who has the belt, he defines what the belt means.

"If you want the belt to be a big prize, you should have a guy who proves his record, who can beat everyone, who is a real martial artist. Not just somebody who does some big things or breaks rules every fight, trying to injure your opponents.

"I respect everybody. I fight clean," Volkov continued. "I fight in a good way, and I'm still best in the game. I don't use any drugs; I'm a clean athlete all my life through martial arts."

The rapidly changing landscape of the heavyweight division, particularly at its peak, has left Volkov in somewhat of a holding pattern. With Tom Aspinall recently vacating the championship , the newly crowned champion Ciryl Gane will defend the belt against Josh Hokit at UFC 334 on Nov. 14 at Madison Square Garden.

Aspinall remains sidelined with eye injuries he suffered against Gane in October 2025. But if he can return sooner rather than later, Volkov fully supports the idea of Aspinall's first fight back being for the recently relinquished title.

That would leave Volkov waiting around even longer, presumably for the winner of the upcoming Alex Pereira vs. Sergei Pavlovich fight set for December.

"It looks like Pereira vs. Pavlovich should be the next closest to a contender fight," Volkov said. "So maybe the winner of this fight should be my next opponent. It looks like that. Nobody else I can see right now [is] in the top rankings who can fight for the belt. Or maybe a fight with Josh Hokit will be also good, just so I can [have] fun with it and have another good week with the UFC."

A mild feud has begun brewing between Volkov and Hokit after Volkov's surprise "praise" of a Hokit title shot earlier this month . In a joking manner, Volkov expressed how kind of the UFC he thought it was to give someone with a "mental illness" a title shot.

Hokit responded on social media shortly after, lambasting Volkov for being boring and saying the Russian should've been released along with former UFC heavyweight contender Jailton Almeida.

Volkov was unsurprised and unamused by the comments, expecting nothing less. Depending on what happens in Hokit's title fight with Gane, Volkov could have his next opponent lined up in the form of "The Incredible Hok."

"He's an adult. He thinks like an elementary school kid. That's it," Volkov said. "This is an answer I could have when I started with my schoolmates. This is not an argument. He fights maybe a grand total of a fight and a half in the organization, and they give him a title shot.

"Again, this just defines what the belt means. Not opposite. ... Maybe I agree — it's not bad. I can still beat everyone in the roster right now in heavyweight. I can do it easily with a smile, confident, doing all the things for the fight week.

"I show everyone I have no problem to make the show or conversation with reporters, whatever. It's better for him to face me in the Octagon, and we'll see who is better."

articles.title: Kayla Allen: From self-taught boxer to star prospect - 'It started in a unique way and it'll finish in a unique way'
articles.summary: Kayla Allen's ascent from using YouTube to teach herself to box in her garden to reaching the GB squad and becoming a star professional prospect is extraordinary; watch Chris Billam-Smith fight Cheavon Clarke on Zuffa Boxing 12 live on Sky Sports on November 7
articles.body:
Her rapid ascent since then has been astonishing. She made it all the way to the GB squad and has now become the first woman to sign with Zuffa Boxing. She will have her second fight on Sky Sports on November 7.

"Any fight I go into, whether it's the first debut, the second fight or a world title fight, everyone's getting dealt with the same," she told Sky Sports .

"It's always been exciting, it's never been boring. So for me it's not about being someone else, it's about being myself, and the best Kayla beats anybody on the night."

After originally pursuing ambitions in football, Allen started trying to box at home during the pandemic lockdown.

"I learned how to box in my back garden as an 18-year-old girl. I watched videos on YouTube, how to throw a jab, watched Mayweather, Mike Tyson, AJ, I just studied the sport and then went down to the local boxing gym, did a couple of white-collar fights and now we're here," Allen said.

"I've always believed in myself. Whenever I first started, no matter what I do I always go: 'I'm going to be the best at this'. So whatever that means I don't know, but that's just my mindset. No matter what I do I'm always the best at it and I'll be the best at boxing."

Her first amateur tournament was the Golden Girl, a large international competition in Sweden. She won it.

Allen performed well in the national championships and was soon on the GB squad, an astonishing ascent.

"Within six months I was on England and then within eight months I was on GB. That's work, credit to my coaches and credit to myself, and the GB system and the England system to allow me to get to where I needed to be. It's a blessing. I'm glad to be here and it's a good opportunity," she said.

It led her now to her breakthrough move into professional boxing, becoming Zuffa's first female signing.

"Where's the girls at? I'm here now, so let's go!" she said. "It helps other females coming through, that nothing's impossible."

She promises: "Explosive, knockouts, just explosive energy, I'm going to bring ferocity to the ring… When I step into that ring it's game on for me.

"It's creating my own legacy, one of one, and creating my own name for female boxing.

"It started in a unique way and it'll finish in a unique way as well. I do everything my own way."

Watch Chris Billam-Smith fight Cheavon Clarke in the main event on Zuffa Boxing 12, live on Sky Sports on November 7.

articles.title: 'I'm better than him everywhere': Renato Moicano sizes up Tom Nolan after Brian Ortega saga
articles.summary: Renato Moicano was scheduled to fight Brian Ortega at UFC 326 in March. Ortega withdrew with injuries.
articles.body: Renato Moicano was scheduled to fight Brian Ortega at UFC 326 in March. Ortega withdrew with injuries. The rematch was booked for UFC 331 in September, only for Ortega to pull out again, this time with a cut above his left eye.Moicano now faces Tom Nolan in the main event at Meta APEX in Las Vegas on October 31 (Nov 1 IST). The Brazilian lightweight has had to prepare for two opponents this year, but his immediate concern is the one who will actually turn up."When I found out about the fight, I changed the game plan. Of course, Brian Ortega is a jiu-jitsu guy, while Tom Nolan is a striker, so I changed my approach to the fight," Moicano told TimesofIndia.com.He has little interest in revisiting the cancellations. "There is nothing I can do about that, you know. The only thing I can do is train, get my weight down and fight on Saturday. I don't think about Brian Ortega," he said.Moicano, 37, is coming off a second-round submission win over Chris Duncan in April, having lost his previous two fights against Beneil Dariush and Islam Makhachev. The Duncan victory stopped that run of defeats. Nolan, 26, has won five consecutive fights, including a unanimous decision over Farès Ziam in June.Moicano is ranked eighth in the UFC lightweight division, with Nolan at No. 12 in the latest rankings. The Australian has never headlined a UFC event before and will be competing over five rounds for the first time in the promotion."I think he's a very dangerous opponent, but I think I'm better than him everywhere," Moicano said.Nolan had called for the fight after beating Ziam. Moicano was not interested in reading too much into the callout."I don't know. I don't care about what they think or what they do. It's just a fight. I have to go over there and beat him, and that's it," he said.A crowded lightweight title pictureThe division has moved on since Moicano's last appearance. Justin Gaethje is the champion after beating Ilia Topuria by fourth-round TKO at UFC Freedom 250 in June. The defeat was the first of Topuria's professional career.Topuria remains No. 1 contender in the UFC rankings, with Arman Tsarukyan at No. 2, Charles Oliveira third, Max Holloway fourth, and Paddy Pimblett fifth. Benoît Saint Denis and Quillan Salkilld are also ahead of Moicano, who needs to keep winning to improve his position.Tsarukyan strengthened his case with a knockout win over Mauricio Ruffy at UFC 331 in September. Oliveira beat Holloway in March, while Pimblett defeated Saint Denis in July. There is no shortage of established names or younger contenders seeking a title opportunity.Moicano has previously said he would welcome a fight against Topuria. The change in the title picture has made the possibility more complicated, with Gaethje now holding the belt and Tsarukyan among the leading candidates for the next shot."Somebody asked me if I would fight Topuria, and I said, of course. But that's up to the UFC. I just have to win my fight and see what happens," Moicano said.Asked whether he needed another major victory before a fight against Topuria became realistic, he did not try to negotiate his way into a matchup."I'm really focused on that fight right now. I think Ilia Topuria could be one, but who knows? I'm not thinking about that right now. I'm just thinking about finishing Tom Nolan and then seeing what's next," he said.A win over Nolan would keep Moicano in the top 10 and give him another result to take into discussions about his next opponent. A loss would leave him needing to rebuild his position while the leading contenders continue to move towards the title.For now, Moicano is not making predictions about the next stage of his career.Asked how he defines success at this point, he offered a straightforward answer. "I think success for me is going over there and finishing Tom Nolan, getting some money, getting back home safe and being ready for the next one," he said.(Moicano faces Nolan at UFC Fight Night, live on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: UFC commits another $1 million to brain-health research in 2026 as WWE and boxing athletes join study running through 2030
articles.summary: UFC is putting another $1 million into research on the long-term effects of repeated head impacts, extending its partnership with Cleveland Clinic through
articles.body: UFC is putting another $1 million into research on the long-term effects of repeated head impacts, extending its partnership with Cleveland Clinic through 2030. Announced on October 8, 2026, the deal also brings WWE into the Professional Athletes Brain Health Study and opens participation to Zuffa Boxing athletes. The research aims to help scientists understand how repeated blows to the head affect athletes over time and what could increase their risk of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE).UFC has supported the study since 2011 and has now committed more than $3 million across four rounds of funding. More than 900 active and retired athletes have enrolled in the program, which offers free brain health assessments, including MRI scans. With WWE and Zuffa Boxing joining the effort, researchers will have a broader group of athletes to study as they investigate brain changes, search for early indicators of injury and explore ways to improve long-term athlete safety.UFC extends its $1 million brain-health commitment through 2030The latest $1 million contribution will support Cleveland Clinic’s Lou Ruvo Center for Brain Health in Las Vegas, Nevada. UFC announced the extension on October 8, 2026, ensuring that its funding for the Professional Athletes Brain Health Study will continue through 2030.UFC first joined the project in 2011, when researchers called it the Professional Fighters Brain Health Study. The original program focused on professional fighters exposed to repeated concussive and sub-concussive impacts. It has since expanded beyond combat sports to include professional bull riders, hockey players and motorsports drivers.The latest contribution marks UFC’s fourth round of financial support. Its total commitment to the research has now exceeded $3 million. Rather than examining athletes at a single point in their careers, the study follows participants over time to track changes in brain health and function.UFC Chief Operating Officer Lawrence Epstein explained the purpose of the renewed commitment in the October 8 announcement.“The research conducted by Dr. Bernick and his team is helping identify early indicators of potential health issues and giving athletes access to information that can help support informed decisions about their health, safety, and long-term well-being during their active careers and beyond,” Epstein said.The research examines the cumulative effects of head impacts, including those that do not result in a diagnosed concussion. That distinction is important because an athlete may experience repeated impacts without an obvious injury after every incident. Researchers want to understand how these exposures affect the brain over the long term.The findings could eventually help athletes and medical teams make better-informed decisions about training, competition and health monitoring. However, the study remains an ongoing research effort, and scientists still need stronger evidence to determine which early changes predict future problems. WWE and Zuffa Boxing join UFC in the expanded research effortThe October 8 announcement also confirmed that WWE and Zuffa Boxing will join the study through athlete participation and financial support. Both organizations operate under TKO Group Holdings, alongside UFC.The expansion brings more athletes into a program that initially focused on professional fighters. Zuffa Boxing athletes are now eligible to participate, while WWE's involvement extends the partnership to another form of combat sports entertainment.WWE President and TKO board member Nick Khan welcomed the expanded collaboration in the October 8 announcement.“Through this partnership with Cleveland Clinic, we can help advance the science of brain health and apply those insights to support future athlete safety,” Khan said.The addition of these organizations gives researchers an opportunity to study athletes with different training demands and exposure to head impacts. Boxers face direct strikes during competition, while professional wrestlers perform physical moves that can involve falls and impacts. Long-term assessments may help researchers understand how different patterns of exposure relate to changes in brain health.However, the announcement did not specify how many WWE or Zuffa Boxing athletes will participate or disclose the individual financial contributions from the two organizations.The study's wider reach also extends beyond professional sports. Its findings could help inform research and safety practices for military personnel and civilians who experience repeated head impacts. Researchers hope that a better understanding of brain changes will support policies that protect people across different environments.More than 900 athletes are helping researchers investigate CTEThe Professional Athletes Brain Health Study is entering its 15th year under Charles Bernick, M.D., senior director of Cognitive Disorders at Cleveland Clinic Nevada and the study's founder and primary investigator.According to the October 8 announcement, the program is the largest study focused on professional athletes exposed to repetitive head trauma. It is also the first to include active and retired male and female athletes together.Participation is voluntary, and athletes receive free, ongoing assessments of brain health and function, including MRI scans. Researchers repeat individual tests annually, allowing them to compare results over several years and look for changes that a single examination might miss.One of the central questions concerns chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or CTE, a degenerative brain disease associated with repeated head trauma. Researchers want to understand how the condition develops, why its effects vary between individuals and which factors could increase a person's risk.Bernick highlighted the value of long-term monitoring in the October 8 announcement.“Following athletes over many years allows us to directly observe how conditions such as CTE develop over time and why long-term outcomes can differ so widely from one individual to another,” he said.Researchers have already detected subtle changes in brain structure and in certain proteins released into the blood following head impacts. These findings could help scientists identify early indicators of brain injury. They do not, however, mean that researchers can currently predict every case of CTE or diagnose the disease in a living athlete through these findings alone.The next phase of the study will examine lifestyle and environmental factors that may influence the development of CTE-related pathology. Investigators also plan to search for more precise predictive or diagnostic biomarkers and begin testing new treatments.The extension through 2030 gives researchers more time to follow athletes and build on the data collected since 2011. For UFC, WWE and Zuffa Boxing, the expanded partnership creates a shared commitment to understanding the health risks associated with repeated head impacts.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 24 wins, seven titles, one heartbreaking defeat: Wrestler Sujeet Kalkal's winning streak ends
articles.summary: Sujeet Kalkal’s wait for a World Championships medal continued as the Indian wrestler suffered a heartbreaking defeat in the men’s 65kg quarterfinals on
articles.body: Sujeet Kalkal’s wait for a World Championships medal continued as the Indian wrestler suffered a heartbreaking defeat in the men’s 65kg quarterfinals on Thursday. Sujeet lost 3-3 on criteria to Tajikistan’s Abdulmazhid Kudiev, bringing his 24-match winning streak to an end.The defeat was a major setback for Sujeet, who had enjoyed an impressive run over the past year. He won seven titles during this period, including the U23 World Championships, the 2026 Asian Championships and the Asian Games.His last defeat before Thursday had come in the repechage round of the World Championships in Zagreb last year. The loss to Kudiev also ended India’s hopes of seeing a second world champion after Sushil Kumar, who won the title in 2010.Kudiev turns the tables on SujeetSujeet had beaten Kudiev in the Asian Games final after making a remarkable comeback. Trailing 2-9, the Indian scored eight straight points to secure the gold medal.However, the Tajik wrestler had the last laugh this time in a closely fought quarterfinal.Sujeet conceded the first point for passivity but moved ahead 2-1 with a takedown just five seconds before the end of the first period. Kudiev was then penalised for passivity, allowing the Indian to increase his lead to 3-1.The contest took a dramatic turn in the final 30 seconds.Sujeet attempted a takedown near the edge of the mat but could not put Kudiev in a danger position. The Tajik wrestler then countered with a takedown of his own.The mat referee did not award Sujeet two points for his move, but the chair umpire gave him the points. Kudiev was also awarded a point for a step-out, leaving Sujeet ahead 5-2.The Tajik corner challenged the decision and won. Sujeet’s two points were cancelled, while Kudiev received two points for his takedown. The score was level at 3-3.Sujeet needed a decisive move in the final seconds but could not find a way past Kudiev. The Tajik wrestler held on to win on criteria because he had scored the last point.Sujeet had started with two convincing winsBefore the quarterfinal, Sujeet had looked in control of his campaign.He opened with a commanding 12-1 win over Switzerland’s Nino Leutert by technical superiority. He then defeated Belarus’ Islam Guseinov 4-0 to reach the quarterfinals.But his winning run ended against the same wrestler he had beaten for Asian Games gold, leaving him still searching for his first senior World Championships title.Tanu enters bronze medal bout, Manisha reaches semifinalsIndia had some positive results in the women’s events, with Tanu Sharma advancing to the bronze medal bout in the 72kg category.Tanu defeated Tunisia’s Zainab Sghaier 5-4 in the repechage round to stay in the medal race. However, Srishti was eliminated after losing her women’s 68kg repechage bout to American Kennedy Blades.Experienced wrestler Manisha Bhanwala moved into the women’s 59kg semifinals with a comfortable 6-0 victory over Mongolia’s Bolortuya Khurelkhuu. Earlier, she had beaten Canada’s Laurence Beauregard by fall.Ahilya wins one bout, Vicky exits in quarterfinalsIn the women’s 55kg category, Ahilya Shinde began with an 8-1 win over Cuba’s Yaynelis Sanz Verdecia. However, she could not hold on to a 3-0 lead against Turkey’s Tuba Demir and went down 6-9.In the men’s 97kg category, Vicky reached the quarterfinals after beating Sarco Colmenarez 8-2 and Radu Letter 10-0.His run ended in the last eight, where Japan’s Arash Yoshida defeated him 12-2 by technical superiority.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jake Paul to make boxing return on Christmas Eve in Dubai with opponent to be revealed
articles.summary: Jake Paul will make his boxing return on Christmas Eve in Dubai, 12 months on from having his jaw broken by Anthony Joshua; his opponent is yet to be confirmed but they say there are plenty of names being discussed
articles.body:
It marks Paul's first fight since he took on former two-time unified heavyweight world champion Anthony Joshua and suffered a broken jaw in the process of a knockout blow in the sixth round.

Back in 2024, he also fought Mike Tyson and has a record of 12-2, with seven KOs since making his professional debut.

On his return to the ring, Paul revealed there are plenty of names in the frame to fight him.

Previous names that have been discussed include former UFC fighters Darren Till and Francis Ngannou, Britain's Chris Eubank Jr and WBC welterweight world champion Ryan Garcia.

"I've spent years proving people wrong, taking risks, and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I'd face," he said.

"Nothing that's happened has changed my belief in myself or what I'm working toward. I'm hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I'm returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey.

"Dubai is a city that thinks big, breaks boundaries, and doesn't believe in limits. That's exactly the kind of place I want to make my comeback.

"We've got plenty of names on the list; let's see who signs the contract. Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody's getting knocked out."

Nakisa Bidarian, co-founder and CEO of Most Valuable Promotions, said: "Jake Paul has spent his career challenging what people think is possible.

"Twelve months ago he suffered a double broken jaw against a two-time heavyweight world champion and since then many have doubted his desire or need to return to boxing.

"Well he is back, and that tells you everything about the competitor Jake Paul is and how much he loves this sport. This is more than a fight.

"We're finalising an opponent worthy of Jake's return and look forward to sharing more in the coming weeks."

articles.title: Jake Paul's Next Fight Announced for Return from Injury After KO Loss to Anthony Joshua
articles.summary: One year after his knockout loss to two-time unified heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua, Jake Paul will be back in the ring.
articles.body:
One year after his knockout loss to two-time unified heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua, Jake Paul will be back in the ring.

Most Valuable Promotions announced on Thursday morning that Paul will make his return on Christmas Eve, headlining a blockbuster event in his first career fight in Dubai. The 29-year-old said he's deciding between "plenty of names" for his next opponent.

"I've spent years proving people wrong, taking risks, and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I'd face. Nothing that's happened has changed my belief in myself or what I'm working toward. I'm hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I'm returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey," Paul said in a release. "Dubai is a city that thinks big, breaks boundaries, and doesn't believe in limits. That's exactly the kind of place I want to make my comeback. We've got plenty of names on the list; let's see who signs the contract. Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody's getting knocked out."

MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian added, "We're finalizing an opponent worthy of Jake's return and look forward to sharing more in the coming weeks."

Paul suffered a broken jaw that required multiple surgeries after his loss to Joshua last December, which marked the first knockout loss of his career.

Months after his fight against Joshua, Paul once said the injury could stop him from ever fighting again, but Bidarian announced earlier this month that the YouTuber was cleared to return. Paul named a long list of potential opponents across boxing and MMA, including Conor McGregor, Canelo Alvarez, Francis Ngannou, Deontay Wilder and Nate Diaz.

Paul has proven long ago to be one of the biggest draws in boxing and a true disruptor in combat sports. Earlier this year, MVP announced a merger with the PFL, creating a new MMA promotion that is expected to launch in 2027.

Paul's return to the ring is sure to draw a large audience later this winter, and fans will be excited to see who he picks as his next opponent.

articles.title: Jake Paul: American to return to ring on 24 December in Dubai
articles.summary: Jake Paul returns to the ring for the first time since losing to Anthony Joshua against a yet to be confirmed opponent on 24 December.
articles.body:
Jake Paul will return to the ring for the first time since losing to Anthony Joshua against a yet to be confirmed opponent on 24 December.

American Paul had two titanium plates fitted and some teeth removed after Joshua broke his jaw during their heavyweight bout in December 2025.

The 29-year-old influencer said in May that his boxing career was "most definitely" in doubt.

Paul will headline a card in Dubai on Christmas Eve, with several names understood to be in contention to be his opponent.

"I've spent years proving people wrong, taking risks, and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I'd face," Paul said.

"Nothing that's happened has changed my belief in myself or what I'm working toward. I'm hungrier than ever.

"We've got plenty of names on the list; let's see who signs the contract. Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody's getting knocked out."

Paul has won 12 of his 14 fights as a professional, with his two defeats coming against Tommy Fury and Joshua.

Nakisa Bidarian, who co-founded Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) with Paul, told the Sun earlier this week that former UFC fighter Darren Till was among the names being considered for the fight in the United Arab Emirates.

"Jake Paul has spent his career challenging what people think is possible," Bidarian said.

"We're finalising an opponent worthy of Jake's return and look forward to sharing more in the coming weeks."

Till, 33, last fought in the UFC in 2022 and made his boxing debut in 2025 - beating Luke Rockhold in his sole professional bout.

The Liverpudlian has since competed in the Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC) and beat Yoel Romero in September.

In July 2025, Paul earned a place in the WBA's cruiserweight rankings after beating former world champion Julio Cesar Chavez Jr, but he lost that ranking in January after defeat by Joshua.

Paul was knocked down twice against the British two-time heavyweight world champion before being stopped in the sixth round in Miami.

articles.body:

Paul (12-2, 7 KOs) last fought in December 2025 against Anthony Joshua, suffering a broken jaw in a sixth-round knockout loss to the former heavyweight champion. Paul was hospitalized after the fight and underwent multiple surgeries during his recovery.

Paul's opponent has not been announced yet.

"I've spent years proving people wrong, taking risks, and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I'd face," Paul said in a press release announcing the fight. "Nothing that's happened has changed my belief in myself or what I'm working toward. I'm hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I'm returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey."

Paul's boxing career began in 2020, with the influencer-turned-fighter winning his first six bouts before losing to Tommy Fury in 2023. Paul went on another six-fight winning streak — including a victory over Mike Tyson — before the loss to Joshua, who was the biggest test in his career to that point.

"Jake Paul has spent his career challenging what people think is possible," MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian said in the release. "Twelve months ago he suffered a double broken jaw against a two-time heavyweight world champion and since then many have doubted his desire or need to return to boxing. Well he is back, and that tells you everything about the competitor Jake Paul is and how much he loves this sport."

The planned Christmas Eve event will come just two weeks after Joshua's next fight, a highly anticipated bout against Tyson Fury on Dec. 11.

articles.title: Canelo Alvarez on his return to boxing after Terence Crawford loss: 'I feel like I'm 26 years old'
articles.summary: More than a year after his loss to Crawford, "Canelo" seeks to reclaim his place atop boxing. But with questions about his age, his future and the dangers su...
articles.body:
Saul "Canelo" Alvarez returns to the ring Saturday after more than a year away, and for those who only casually follow the journey of boxing's biggest star , one word may come to epitomize his fight against WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli: Redemption.

Canelo, 36, is a veteran of 68 pro fights. His longtime trainer, Eddy Reynoso, has insisted to Uncrowned before that Alvarez fought at least 10 more during his teenage years in Mexico, but those remain unlisted by boxing's data-keepers, even if they've lobbied to have them included on his record. Regardless, he's battle-tested and battle-hardened.

Unusually durable. Occasionally destructive. Alvarez is renowned as much for his wars with Gennadiy Golovkin as he is for breaking the jaws of lesser foes, like Billy Joe Saunders in 2021, or, if Ulises Solis is to be believed, outside the ring in 2011 too .

The risk in competing in the kinds of fights Canelo has taken on is that losses become a reality. Canelo has three of them: To Floyd Mayweather, Dmitry Bivol, and Terence Crawford, the latter of whom beat him last year in Las Vegas . Alvarez hasn't fought since.

He had arthroscopic surgery on his left elbow in late October 2025, approximately six weeks after his unanimous decision defeat to "Bud." During his recovery, he said he was thinking solely about boxing and how he can win back the world titles he lost to Crawford.

This Saturday at the Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, he gets the chance to claim one of them back.

It would be easy, then, to reduce Alvarez's journey back to the ring as one of redemption, as so many likely will. But, really, it's about so much more.

It's about a loss of control, and whether Canelo has really regained any within the sport he has dedicated his life to.

It's about a man who was once in complete control inside the ring; a fighter who had control over what happened to an opponent's body, now contemplating whether he has lost a step. Worse, whether he's lost his mental edge.

Immediately after losing to Crawford, Canelo conceded that, despite trying, "your body just can't take it anymore."

"Reynoso was telling me everything I needed to do," he said at the time, "and I tried. But my body wasn't responding. I had cramps in my legs."

Yet it wasn't just about losing control over a physique that had, for decades, been his edge. Yes, he was stocky. Resilient. Economical. But against Crawford, there was more.

"When you lose, you always look back at your mistakes," Alvarez told Uncrowned ahead of Saturday's return. "At this level, there's very little between a win and a loss. I did a good job of preparing for that fight, but throughout fight week my mind wasn't there."

Those around Canelo suggest the 13-month break since has only benefited him.

In DAZN's recent documentary, "Saul — The Return of Canelo Alvarez" , Reynoso described his fighter as "recharged" following the defeat: "He is more motivated with unfinished business. That's what has driven him to work harder for this fight."

There are consequences to working hard in the gym today that were absent from Canelo's prime, though. "He gets tired because he's human," Reynoso said.

"I hope more than anything to win the fight and show that we can still be relevant in boxing."

"Saul soon will turn 37," he finished. "It's no secret that we are in our last fights."

Canelo may feel different. He is, after all, one of the sport's most stubborn men. He's determined to win each of his world titles back, one by one, starting with Mbilli on Saturday. And, when speaking to him, there is never a question whether his heart is still in the game. "I love boxing," Alvarez told Uncrowned.

"I enjoy boxing a lot and I always give 100% in the gym because I really love what I do. Boxing is my passion."

"I feel like I'm 26 years old," he added. "I believe in that. I'm [going to] show Mbilli what level of fighter he's facing."

If Mbilli were fighting Canelo when the Mexican was actually 26, when he knocked Liam Smith out with a body shot, there would be little question that the hulking Canada-based bruiser would fall too.

But this is a different Canelo. This is a Canelo who hasn't scored a knockout in the past five years, not since he stopped Caleb Plant in the 11th round in November 2021.

Alvarez insists he's recovered from the Crawford loss, from the surgery, and from accumulated wear and tear. And though he is one of the sport's biggest names, he even linked up with fellow modern-day pound-for-pound great Oleksandr Usyk after relocating his camp to Spain for this comeback.

"He came for two to three days [to the gym] and I enjoyed it a lot. I appreciate them for leading my training in the gym," Alvarez said of the collaborative work with team Usyk. "I used their people for strength and conditioning. They helped us, Eddy and me.

"Usyk is [funny]," he added. "We talked and you realize why he's the champion he is. The mentality is everything."

It is an old adage that fights are already won or lost before either fighter even steps through the ropes and hears the opening bell.

Canelo himself concedes his fight week mentality before boxing Crawford left a lot to be desired. And his preparations for Mbilli, in Riyadh, could also have been smoother.

The Saudi Arabian capital, you see, has been subjected to repeated missile attacks from Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels throughout October . It comes amid escalating conflict between the Houthis and Saudi-backed forces.

The Houthis targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, killing 13 people and injuring more than 300 in an attack on Oct. 10, prompting its closure and throwing international travel into disarray .

Tennis and golf events in the region were postponed.

Alvarez's fight with Mbilli, though, remained on the calendar.

One of the sport's central financiers, Turki Alalshikh, said earlier this month that Alvarez "fears nothing," while insisting the show would go on.

But the Houthis have warned that Riyadh's airport remains a military target, leaving the region under the threat of further attacks just days before Canelo and Mbilli are due to fight 20 miles away.

And so you cannot help but wonder whether this is yet another situation that is out of Alvarez's control, and if it has affected his training, his mindset, or both.

"I see a beautiful Riyadh," Canelo said upon his arrival in Saudi Arabia . "I saw in the media a lot of things [about the attacks], but I was confident of coming to Riyadh … I feel safe, like in my own home. I don't see anything bad."

Canelo has tried for more than a year to recapture the control he's long had over his mind, his body, and his destiny.

On Saturday, against Mbilli, he will discover how much of it remains in his own hands.

articles.title: Sean O'Malley: Song Yadong could 'definitely' beat Merab Dvalishvili
articles.summary: Sean O'Malley sees Song Yadong as a tough matchup for Merab Dvalishvili.
articles.body:
Sean O'Malley sees Song Yadong as a tough matchup for Merab Dvalishvili .

Dvalishvili (21-6 MMA, 14-4 UFC) was outlasted by bantamweight champion Petr Yan (21-5 MMA, 13-4 UFC) in this past Saturday's UFC 333 co-main event at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. Song (24-9-1 MMA, 13-4-1 UFC), who's coming off a knockout of Umar Nurmagomedov , was in attendance for the fight.

O'Malley (20-3 MMA, 12-3 UFC) is also campaigning for the next title shot. If he does get his wish, he expects Dvalishvili and Song to potentially fight next.

"Merab was getting in on those takedowns (vs. Yan) for the first 10 minutes," O'Malley said in an interview with Bradley Martyn . "Not getting takedowns, but he was getting into his waist, dragging him to the mat, Petr was having to scramble. But then, as the fight went on, Petr's guard is so – he's so short, he's so little, his guard is down here.

"So, when he (Dvalishvili) shoots, it's easy to defend for him. It was so sick to watch. Merab's a motherf*cker, but Song Yadong could beat Merab, too. Song is the same size as those little f*ckers, and he's explosive as f*ck. He's hard to take down, he hits hard. If Song and Merab fight next, Song could definitely win."

O'Malley beat Yan in a close fight at UFC 280 . He has high praise for Yan's skills, but is confident he's the guy to dethrone him .

"I'm excited to rewatch that fight," O'Malley added. "I rewatched their second fight a few times. I'm excited to rewatch this fight, but Petr is so good. He's probably up there pound-for-pound No. 1."

articles.title: Robert Whittaker picks Alexander Volkanovski to beat Justin Gaethje in potential fight
articles.summary: Former middleweight champ Robert Whittaker thinks Alexander Volkanovski would beat Justin Gaethje.
articles.body:
Featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski wants another crack at winning the lightweight title. "The Great" has proposed a mega-fight against lightweight champ Justin Gaethje and UFC CEO Dana White is open to the idea.

Volkanovski successfully defended his belt at UFC 333 on Oct. 24 defeating the previously undefeated contender Movsar Evloev via second-round stoppage. It was the second title defense of the 38-year old's second 145-pound championship reign.

Gaethje hasn't fought since defeating Ilia Topuria to capture the lightweight title at the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House in June. If the two do get matched up against each other, former middleweight champ Robert Whittaker believes Volkanovski would get the job done.

"I want to see him fight Gaethje. I want to see him fight Gaethje because, dude, he beats Gaethje," Whittaker said on the MMArcade Podcast . "He beats him, man. 100% he does."

Volkanovski stated that he'd retire if given the opportunity to face "The Highlight." He suggested it could be the final fight for he and Gaethje. Whittaker likes the possibility.

"And that is such a cool thing that both guys leave it all out there. Both guys leave gloves out there. Both guys cement legacies. That's mad. That's a really cool end of the rainbow sort of situation," said the former champ.

articles.title: Daniel Dubois: Joseph Parker on shortlist for WBO heavyweight champion's next world title defence
articles.summary: Daniel Dubois is considering opponents for his next world title defence which include Joseph Parker; Dubois was due to fight Parker in February 2025, but was forced to withdraw due to illness; Parker can continue career after suspension lifted following a failed drug test
articles.body:
Parker was due to challenge Dubois for the IBF world heavyweight title last February, but was forced to withdraw due to illness in the week of the fight.

Dubois could now resume his rivalry with Parker, who announced in August that he will continue his career after a suspension was lifted following a failed drug test in October 2025.

The New Zealander is being considered as a possible next fight for Dubois, who has other options after stopping Fabio Wardley in the second round of their rematch earlier this month.

Dubois has told Sky Sports that he wants the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua winner or unification fights against WBC titlist Agit Kabayel or IBF belt-holder Filip Hrgovic.

"Any one of them [next]. Hrgovic, he was there on Saturday, maybe him or Kabayel," he said. "Hrgovic was tough as well, Kabayel, we'll see, we'll see what he's about. He ain't been in with a guy like me but he's a good fighter.

"Just anyone with a damn belt… anyone who wants it."

UK Anti-Doping officially confirmed that Parker was free to return to the ring in the summer as details of the case were shared which revealed how Parker stated that the failed drugs test was caused by exposure to cocaine being used by his nutritionist.

The 34-year-old had a spell as WBO champion from 2016-2018, and had rejuvenated his career with wins over Deontay Wilder, Zhilei Zhang and Martin Bakole before his loss to Wardley.

articles.title: Tyson Fury Netflix Documentary Trailer, Release Date Announced Ahead of Anthony Joshua Fight
articles.summary: Just over one month away from his highly-anticipated showdown with Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury is getting the documentary treatment from Netflix on Nov. 27.
articles.body:
Just over one month away from his highly-anticipated showdown with Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury is getting the documentary treatment from Netflix on Nov. 27.

The streamer released the trailer for the aptly-titled doc TYSON FURY on Thursday, along with the announcement it will be released on Thanksgiving weekend.

The official description on the trailer's YouTube page notes the documentary will include "exclusive access" to Fury, his wife Paris and his father John.

Snippets from the trailer include Fury's childhood, his 2015 showdown with Wladimir Klitschko, his struggles with addiction and mental health.

The film, directed by Lucy Wilcox, is the latest venture between Fury and Netflix. He was also in the docuseries At Home with the Furys that has aired two seasons for the streamer with a third expected at some point in 2027.

Fury vs. Joshua from Principality Stadium will also be broadcast worldwide by Netflix on Dec. 11.

articles.title: Jake Paul anuncia su regreso al boxeo... ¡un día antes de Navidad!
articles.standfirst: El influencer y boxeador estadounidense volverá a subirse al ring un año después de ser noqueado por Anthony Joshua
articles.summary: El influencer y boxeador estadounidense volverá a subirse al ring un año después de ser noqueado por Anthony Joshua
articles.body: Jake Paul está de vuelta. El influencer y púgil estadounidense recibió un severo K.O. por parte de Anthony Joshua el 19 de diciembre de 2025 que le fracturó la mandíbula, y tras someterse a varias operaciones ha anunciado su regreso para el próximo 24 de diciembre en Dubái. Muchos daban su carrera por acabada, por lo que este anuncio ha pillado por sorpresa al mundo del boxeo, con su rival todavía por confirmarse. A través de un comunicado, Paul ha afirmado que está listo para volver a callar bocas, después de mostrar su valentía al subirse a un ring contra uno de los pesos pesados más temibles del panorama como es Joshua. En esta ocasión no se sabe si bajará el listón o buscará otro gran nombre del circuito profesional, pero lo que está claro es que todas las miradas estarán puestas en él para ver en qué condiciones está después de la derrota más dura de su carrera. "Todo lo que quiero para Nochebuena es boxear en Dubái. He pasado años demostrando que la gente se equivoca, tomando riesgos y poniéndome a prueba contra oponentes que nadie pensó que enfrentaría. Nada de lo que ha pasado ha cambiado mi creencia en mí mismo ni en lo que estoy trabajando. Estoy más hambriento que nunca, y el jueves 24 de diciembre, regresaré al ring en Dubái para comenzar el próximo capítulo de mi viaje. Dubái es una ciudad que piensa en grande, rompe barreras y no cree en límites. Ese es exactamente el tipo de lugar en el que quiero hacer mi regreso. Tenemos un montón de nombres en la lista; veamos quién firma el contrato. Feliz Navidad, Dubái. Santa Paul viene al pueblo, y alguien va a recibir un nocaut". Lo cierto es que la carrera del estadounidense ha ido de menos a más con el paso de los años. Tras hacerse conocido en el mundo de internet siendo un adolescente, Jake decidió dar el salto al boxeo en 2018, y desde entonces no ha parado de realizar combates. Al principio sus enfrentamientos eran ante ex jugadores de baloncesto como Nate Robinson, o ex peleadores de la UFC como Ben Askren, Nate Díaz, Tyron Woodley o Anderson Silva, pero poco a poco fue subiendo el nivel. Muchos criticaban a Jake al elegir a peleadores de menor tamaño que él para poder lucir mejor, y la gota que colmó el vaso fue su combate ante Mike Tyson en noviembre de 2024, lo que muchos consideraron una falta de respeto teniendo en cuenta que 'Iron' llevaba mucho tiempo sin subirse a un ring. Poco tiempo después también superó a otro gran ex boxeador como Julio César Chávez Jr., pero de nuevo volvió a estar en el punto de mira al no medirse a boxeadores activos. Todo esto se acabó hace poco menos de un año, cuando anunció que se mediría a Anthony Joshua, y pagó las consecuencias. Una derecha del británico rompió la mandíbula de Jake, que pasó de ser una superestrella a un meme, y desde entonces ha estado recuperándose para volver más fuerte. En dos meses volverá a ser su momento, por lo que solo queda saber quién será el indicado para ponerle a prueba de nuevo.

articles.title: Fedor Emelianenko Comments on Francis Ngannou Fight Rumors
articles.summary: Legendary MMA heavyweight Fedor Emelianenko commented on rumors that he could be fighting Francis Ngannou.The 50-year-old Emelianenko has not fought since a...
articles.body:
Legendary MMA heavyweight Fedor Emelianenko commented on rumors that he could be fighting Francis Ngannou.

The 50-year-old Emelianenko has not fought since a first-round TKO loss to Ryan Bader at Bellator 290 in February 2023. However, that has not stopped the rumor mill from matching him up against Ngannou in a battle between two of the top heavyweight free agents in MMA.

So, could this dream fight actually happen?

Fedor Emelianenko Open to Boxing Francis Ngannou

Speaking to Ushatayka, Emelianenko said that while he's interested in fighting Ngannou, it would have to be in boxing, as he believes he has dealt with too many injuries for this to currently be a viable matchup in mixed martial arts.

"If we're talking about a real dream, I'd be interested in fighting Francis Ngannou under boxing rules. I couldn't manage MMA now because I have too many injuries, but I'd have a go at him in boxing. That's just me thinking out loud. I never said we were in negotiations," Emelianenko said.

One promotion that Emelianenko never fought for was the UFC, as he was never able to agree to terms with UFC president Dana White to fight inside the Octagon.

While Emelianenko was a free agent several times in his career, he signed with promotions like Bellator MMA and Strikeforce instead of the UFC.

But according to Emelianenko, while it appears from the outside that White was not interested in signing him, the legendary Russian says that White did want to bring him into the Octagon, but every time he reached out to him, Emelianenko was under contract with another organization, and thus he couldn't fight in the UFC whenever White tried to sign him.

"He (Dana) came over saying he wanted me to fight for him, but one fight earlier I'd been a free agent. I was free, and they didn't sign me. It happened every time. When I'm free, they aren't interested. When I'm under contract, the offers start coming. But if you're under contract, you can't sign another one. There would be legal proceedings," Emelianenko said.

articles.title: Robert Whittaker: Alexander Volkanovski '100 percent' beats Justin Gaethje
articles.summary: Robert Whittaker backs Alexander Volkanovski in his pursuit of a second UFC belt.
articles.body:
Robert Whittaker backs Alexander Volkanovski in his pursuit of a second UFC belt.

Volkanovski (29-4 MMA, 16-3 UFC) set his eyes on a superfight with lightweight champion Justin Gaethje (28-5 MMA, 11-5 UFC) after he retained his featherweight title with a second-round TKO of Movsar Evloev Saturday at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi.

Volkanovski pitched a double retirement idea against Gaethje and Whittaker supports his suggestion.

"I want to see him fight Gaethje," Whittaker said of Volkanovski on his MMArcade Podcast . "I want to see him fight Gaethje because, dude, he beats Gaethje. He beats him, man – 100 percent, he does. And that is such a cool thing that both guys leave it all out there, both guys leave gloves out there, both guys cement legacies. That's mad. That's a really cool end of the rainbow sort of situation."

The odds for Volkanovski vs. Evloev were a pick'em, with many doubting the 38-year-old champion because of his age. With wins over Evloev, Jose Aldo, Diego Lopes twice and Max Holloway three times, Whittaker is surprised to see Volkanovski continuously get underestimated.

"I think everyone in that division doesn't realize how good Volk is until he's standing across from them," Whittaker said. "That's the truth of it. We've seen a lot of good guys riding a lot of momentum going into those fights – people like Max Holloway standing opposite side him and not realizing how good Volk is. Let's be honest: The world didn't realize how good he is until he keeps repeatedly doing the same thing over and over and over, and working people."

articles.title: Volkanovski valora la idea de subir al peso ligero... ¡y pelear contra Tsarukyan!
articles.standfirst: En caso de que Gaethje se retira, el campeón de peso pluma quiere dejar vacante su cinturón y enfrentarse al armenio
articles.summary: En caso de que Gaethje se retira, el campeón de peso pluma quiere dejar vacante su cinturón y enfrentarse al armenio
articles.body: Alexander Volkanovski tiene decidido abandonar la división de peso pluma y dejar vacante su cinturón para intentar por última vez ser doble campeón de la UFC en peso ligero. Tras noquear a Movsar Evloev en el UFC 333, el peleador australiano considera que no tiene muchos más retos en las 145 libras, por lo que su intención es subir de categoría para pelear por el título. De hecho, en caso de que Justin Gaethje -campeón indiscutido- se retire, ha afirmado que estaria dispuesto a medirse por el título vacante ante Arman Tsarukyan. Gaethje sigue indeciso en cuanto a qué decisión tomar respecto a su futuro. Tras finalizar a Ilia Topuria en el UFC Casa Blanca y cumplir el sueño de toda una carrera, existe la posibilidad de que el peleador estadounidense decida colgar las guantillas sin llegar a defender el título. Tsarukyan ha revelado que la compañía le ha prometido que será el siguiente contendiente al cinturón, y Volkanovski estaría dispuesto a medirse a él si no puede enfrentarse a 'The Highlight'. En un principio, 'The Great' había propuesto un combate de retiro con Gaethje en el que pasase lo que pasase ambos pondrían fin a sus carreras, pero ahora también ha hablado de un plan B. "Dejaré vacante el cinturón de peso pluma y me enfrentaré a Arman Tsarukyan por el título. Así de sencillo. Si fuera campeón de peso ligero, me enfrentarían a Arman. Al 100% si Gaethje no quiere, lo haré yo. Eso me entusiasma", afirmó en una entrevista con Ariel Helwani. El peleador australiano cree que el grappling de Tsarukyan no sería suficiente para frenarle, ya que fue capaz de contener la lucha de Islam Makhachev y no cree que el armenio le vaya a suponer una amenaza mayor. Además, en caso de ir al suelo afirma que sería capaz de volver a levantarse, y aunque respeta el striking de Arman no cree que esté a su altura. Lo que está claro es que Volkanovski está haciendo todo lo posible por que la UFC le permita subir de categoría. Ha propuesto el combate con Gaethje, una posible revancha con Topuria y ahora ha afirmado que incluso se enfrentarían a Tsarukyan. 'Volk' sabe que le quedan uno o dos combates más antes de retirarse, por lo que su objetivo es el doble cinturón a toda costa. Dana White ya ha afirmado que le concedería al australiano esa oportunidad de nuevo después de lo mucho que ha ayudado a la compañía, por lo que ahora está por ver cómo se encajan todas las piezas del puzzle. Volkanovski, Tsarukyan, Gaethje, Topuria, Pimblett... Muchos nombres y un solo cinturón en juego.

articles.title: El campeón Mbilli ve a Canelo en declive y lo da por sentenciado
articles.standfirst: El francés cree que es el mejor momento para vérselas con el excampeón absoluto de la categoría
articles.summary: El francés cree que es el mejor momento para vérselas con el excampeón absoluto de la categoría
articles.body: Saúl ‘Canelo’ Álvarez (63-3-2, 39 KOs) se mide este sábado al campeón invicto Christian ‘Sólido’ Mbilli (29-0-1, 24 KOs) en Riad. Pese a su casi impecable historial –empató contra Lester Martínez en su última pelea-, el francés de origen camerunés tiene por delante el mayor reto de su carrera, pues jamás se ha enfrentado a un rival de la calidad y experiencia del mexicano. El fornido francés, que llega como campeón del supermedio por el Consejo Mundial de Boxeo (WBC) tras renunciar Crawford al cinturón, todavía no ha realizado nunca una defensa pero se siente favorito y considera que su rival ya está en declive. “Nadie mejora recibiendo puñetazos en la cara durante más de 20 años", declaró a ‘talkSPORT’ el boxeador camerunés de nacimiento y ahora afincado en Canadá. ‘Sólido’ además argumentó por qué ve a Canelo, de 36 años, en regresión: “Tal vez sea por su potencia o simplemente por su capacidad de golpeo, pero tipos como [Jaime] Munguia o [Edgar] Berlanga están llegando hasta el final y teniendo buenos momentos ahora. Y yo no soy como esos tipos, así que, siendo honesto y realista, ahora es el momento perfecto para que luche contra él. Espero poder romperle la barbilla, y acepté la pelea para hacerlo". Ya durante la conferencia de prensa en Riad de hoy, ni uno ni otro han estado demasiado elocuentes, pero Álvarez ha mandado un recado: “¿Por qué Mbilli? Porque no creo en los caminos cortos y yo siempre voy contra los campeones, es la mejor pelea ahora”. El tapatío hace ya más de un año que peló contra Crawford y se las verá contra un rival muy rocoso, pero menos técnico que él, circunstancia que tendría que aprovechar.

articles.title: Roman Reigns inspired his punches; Andre Russell earned him a nickname: Meet Army havaldar and Asian Games medallist Kapil Pokhariya
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Jumping on cotton-filled mattresses, punching pillows, throwing them over walls and hitting a homemade punching bag filled with mountain soil -
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Jumping on cotton-filled mattresses, punching pillows, throwing them over walls and hitting a homemade punching bag filled with mountain soil - Kapil Pokhariya’s childhood was all about pro-wrestling.His fascination with pro-wrestler Roman Reigns was well known in his locality. He would skip meals, playtime, and outings to watch WWE programming on television. Once the show was over, he would try to copy the moves and punches at home.Little did he know that this childhood fascination could one day bring him his biggest recognition.Today, Kapil - an Indian Army havaldar - is an Asian Games medallist. Kapil won bronze in the men’s 90kg boxing event at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.“I never knew that copying Roman Reigns and practising those punches would bring me this far. I used to save recordings of his videos, and I still have them. I am really proud of where I am today. Honestly, I started learning how to throw punches by copying Roman Reigns (laugh),” Kapil told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview."My favourite was WrestleMania and Money in the Bank," he said.From Khatima to the Asian Games podiumKapil hails from Chakarpur village in Khatima, Uttarakhand, far from the major boxing centres that have produced several Indian stars.His father, Narendra Singh Pokhariya, served in the Indian Army. He wanted his son to study well and join the Army as a commissioned officer. Boxing, however, was never part of the original plan.Narendra often watched his son copy WWE stars at home. Initially, he would scold and even beat him for damaging things around the house. But his view slowly changed when he saw Kapil putting sand into a thick sack after returning from school and punching it with all his strength.“A teacher used to teach boxing at a nearby school. I saw the students punching a bag and decided to make one myself. My father scolded me in the beginning, but later he took me to a training centre and got me admitted there. That is how I got into boxing,” Kapil said.From a small training ground to the boxing ringKapil did not begin his boxing journey at a big academy. His first steps came at a small training ground, where he practised alongside boys of his age and those who were older. After a few months, he began training under a coach.“I come from a small village where boxing was never a popular sport. Pooran Bohra sir was there. He trained a small group of boys for just a few hours on selected days of the week. But I was interested in learning. I listened to him carefully and repeated everything he taught me when I returned home,” Kapil said.With time, Kapil developed as a boxer and competed in his first state-level competition in 2015. He went into the tournament with excitement but came away disappointed. His first competitive bout ended in defeat in the opening round.“I was really disappointed. It was the first bout of my life, and I was seeing such a large crowd for the first time. I lost in the first round. But that competition and the defeat taught me a lot. My interest in boxing grew even stronger after that,” he said.Kapil returned with a different mindset at the national-level competition. This time, he did more than win his bouts - he also claimed the gold medal. The prize money was followed by a job in the Indian Army. He joined the force in April 2017 and was appointed as a havaldar. His boxing career took a big step forward after that.The Army gave him opportunities to improve his skills and compete at a higher level. He began training more seriously, took part in Services competitions, won medals and continued to grow as a boxer.“My father wanted me to study and join the Army as a commissioned officer. He joined as a sepoy and retired as a havaldar. But he wanted me to reach a higher rank if I joined the Indian Army,” Kapil said.“He was very happy. The day I won a national medal, he hugged me. That was when I realised that I had achieved something big in my life,” Kapil said.“Now, after winning this Asian Games medal, I will be promoted to naib subedar. Papa said, ‘Ab tu mera senior ho gaya hai’,” the Indian boxer recalled with a smile.The ‘Andre Russell’ of KhatimaLike many children in India, Kapil also grew up playing gully cricket. He even played inter-village cricket in Uttarakhand.His height, muscular build and powerful hitting made him a popular figure on the local cricket grounds. His ability to hit big sixes earned him the nickname ‘Russell’, after West Indies power-hitter Andre Russell.“I loved Andre Russell. I also liked Hardik Pandya. People used to call me ‘Khatima ka Russell’ because of my power. The boys wanted me in their team because I could hit big sixes,” he said, laughing.The Road Ahead and LA 2028 DreamFor Kapil, the Asian Games bronze is only the beginning. His biggest dream is to represent India at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and win a medal.Under the Boxing Federation of India's selection criteria, Asian Games medallists will be selected as the main entries in their respective weight categories for the 2027 World Boxing Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan. The tournament is scheduled for April and will be the first qualifying event in boxing for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.Kapil knows there is still a long road ahead. “Rukna nahi hai ab, bas aage dekhna hai,” he said.“The Olympics is the ultimate dream. I want to go there, represent my country and win a medal. That is the only thing on my mind right now. I am preparing for the World Championships in April,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jake Paul capable of beating Anthony Joshua with right preparation, according to MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian
articles.summary: MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian claims Jake Paul could beat Anthony Joshua were the pair to fight again; Paul announced this week he will return to the ring in Dubai on December 24 for the first time since fighting Joshua
articles.body:
Paul made the most daunting step-up of his crossover career last December when he faced former two-time heavyweight world champion Joshua, who broke the jaw of his opponent in a sixth-round stoppage victory.

Paul was required to have some teeth removed and had two titanium plates put in his mouth such was the damage caused by Joshua.

Joshua later overcame two first-round knockdowns to beat Albanian heavyweight Kristian Prenga, and is now gearing up to face Tyson Fury in a long-awaited all-British showdown at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11.

"I was pretty vocal that I didn't want him to do the fight on three weeks' notice," said MVP chief executive Bidarian of Paul's fight with Joshua.

"He did better than the guy Anthony Joshua fought in July [Prenga] and was not KO'd.

"I don't think it was a massive overshoot, Jake landed quite a few times on AJ and you saw in July AJ is vulnerable but it was too fast, not enough prep time.

"He was cutting weight to fight Gervonta Davis and then suddenly fighting a guy who was 40lbs naturally heavier than him.

"If Jake had to do that with the right training camp he'd have a really good shot at beating AJ."

Paul announced this week he will return to the ring against an unnamed opponent in Dubai on Christmas Eve, his first scheduled bout since facing Joshua.

Darren Till is among the possible opponents as Paul looks to bolster a resume already including Mike Tyson, Julio César Chávez Jr, Nate Diaz and Joshua.

"One of the things Jake said last week was, 'I'm a bigger dog than I've ever been because none of those punches actually hurt, sure he broke my jaw and I fell down but if you saw my face I said woah, that was a zinger, that felt good'.

"Tell me who else breaks their jaw in two places, stands in the ring and does and interview for 10 minutes talking about the fight. That's who the warrior Jake Paul is."

Bidarian explained that the shortlist of potential fights for Paul is now at three or four names, with a view to announcing the opponent in the next fortnight.

"We are down to three or four names, just trying to see ultimately who we get across the finish line," he told Sky Sports News .

"Darren [Till] is definitely somebody we've had on the list. There are two or three names that are still under consideration.

"It's going to be exciting, and, as every Jake Paul fight is, an even match-up. Every step Jake has taken based on experience or level has been evenly matched and he's come through, other than the fight against Anthony Joshua, he has come through with flying colours.

"Thirteen months ago, he pressed me on fighting Anthony Joshua within a three-week window, he pressed me he could beat him.

"He was knocked down, TKO'd, broken jaw in two places and now he's back after a year off so just trying to manage the right opponent who has commercial viability, who is a true test but who doesn't have a massive advantage versus Jake Paul.

"I'm hoping whether it's next week or week after we'll announce who that opponent is."

articles.title: Paul Heyman reveals what derailed Brock Lesnar’s UFC career
articles.summary: Regarded as one of the top professional wrestlers in the industry, Brock Lesnar has also experienced a successful sporting career in multiple other industrie...
articles.body:
Regarded as one of the top professional wrestlers in the industry, Brock Lesnar has also experienced a successful sporting career in multiple other industries. A former NFL player as well as a successful UFC fighter , Lesnar has done it all.

Done with his NFL and UFC careers a long time ago, Lesnar recently retired from WWE after losing to Oba Femi at WWE SummerSlam 2026. WWE Hall of Famer and Lesnar's WWE manager Paul Heyman recently appeared for an interview with Graham Bensinger, where he was asked about his relationship with "The Beast Incarnate."

Heyman heaped praise on Lesnar before claiming that Lesnar's battle with diverticulitis ruined his UFC career. "It's one of those things, it's just magic. It's lightning in a bottle. He was my Aryan, and I was his Jew. His name was perfect, what a name. Brock Lesnar, you don't have to make up a name. He is the greatest athlete on the face of the planet and the only reason why he doesn't get the credit he deserves is number one, there is a preconceived notion of what a professional wrestler is.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Number two, because diverticulitis robbed him of so much more great athletic accomplishment. If he didn't have diverticulitis, he would've never been defeated in UFC. Never. He'd still be champion today at 49. There's nobody on this planet that could hang with him, no one. No one would get out of the first round with him, there's no way," Heyman said.

After a short run in NJPW, Lesnar began his MMA career. After just one fight for Hero in 2007, Lesnar jumped ships and joined UFC in 2008. He remained a part of the UFC till 2011, and was even the UFC World Heavyweight Champion there. After losing to Cain Velasquez and Alistair Overeem and struggling with diverticulitis, Lesnar decided to retire from the sport in 2011. He later returned for another fight against Mark Hunt in 2016.

articles.title: Manisha Bhanwala creates history, becomes India's first-ever women's world wrestling champion
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian wrestling has a new history-maker!
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian wrestling has a new history-maker! Manisha Bhanwala produced a sensational performance to clinch the gold medal in the women's 59kg category at the World Wrestling Championships on Friday, becoming India's first-ever women's world champion.In a breathtaking gold medal bout, Manisha overturned a daunting 0-6 deficit to defeat Pan American champion Abigail Nette 8-6. Refusing to surrender despite falling behind early, the Indian wrestler mounted a remarkable comeback to turn the contest on its head and secure a historic victory.The triumph marks a landmark moment for Indian wrestling, particularly for the women's game, which has steadily strengthened its presence on the international stage.Manisha's achievement also ends India's 16-year wait for a senior world champion. The country's last world title had come through Sushil Kumar, who won gold at the 2010 World Wrestling Championships.Her victory comes after a memorable campaign for Indian women's wrestling in Astana, Kazakhstan. Neelam Sirohi (50kg) and Kajal Dhochak (76kg) had already scripted history by reaching the finals and securing silver medals. It was the first time two Indian women had competed in finals at the same edition of the senior World Championships.Until this edition, Anshu Malik's silver medal in the 57kg category at the 2021 World Championships in Oslo had stood alone as an Indian woman's runner-up finish at the senior championships.Neelam and Kajal changed that narrative with their impressive double-silver finish. Manisha has now taken the breakthrough a step further, becoming the first Indian woman to win a world title at the senior championships.Trailing by six points against Nette, Manisha displayed extraordinary resilience and determination to fight her way back into contention. Her 8-6 victory will be remembered as one of the defining moments in Indian women's wrestling.From Neelam and Kajal's historic silver medals to Manisha's golden triumph, Indian women wrestlers have delivered a powerful statement on the world stage.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: WBC middleweight champions Adames to face Warburton in non-title bout
articles.summary: WBC middleweight world champion Carlos Adames makes his Zuffa Boxing debut against Welshman Gerome Warburton on Saturday, 14 November.
articles.body:
WBC middleweight world champion Carlos Adames will make his Zuffa Boxing debut against Welshman Gerome Warburton on Saturday, 14 November, but his title will not be at stake.

Adames is to face Warburton in a headline 165-pound (11st 11lb, 74.8kg) catchweight bout in Zuffa Boxing's first event held in Saudi Arabia.

The 32-year-old, whose record is 25-1-1, will step into the ring for the first fight since defending his title against Austin 'Ammo' Williams in March.

Warburton, who boasts an 18-2-2 professional record, takes on the once-beaten Dominican after a decision win in Nathan Heaney's retirement match in September.

The Colwyn Bay middleweight defended his WBA continental title by beating Heaney and has previously stated his desire for a world title fight.

Warburton will have to wait longer for that opportunity, as Adames will not put his WBC strap on the line in Riyadh.

Australian boxer Jason Moloney will also make his Zuffa debut against Mexico's Andres Teran in a 10-round bantamweight co-main event.

articles.title: Giro para la próxima semana en UFC: Cortés-Acosta vs Johnny Walker, nuevo Main Event
articles.standfirst: Tras la baja de Sean Brady en su combate ante Gabriel Bonfim, serán los dos pesos pesados los que protagonicen el nuevo combate estelar
articles.summary: Tras la baja de Sean Brady en su combate ante Gabriel Bonfim, serán los dos pesos pesados los que protagonicen el nuevo combate estelar
articles.body: La Fight Night de UFC que se celebrará el próximo 7 de noviembre en el META Apex de Las Vegas ha sufrido un cambio inesperado en las últimas horas. En un principio, el combate estelar de la cartelera iba a ser el duelo entre Sean Brady y Gabriel Bonfim en el peso wélter, pero una infección del estaodunidense ha provocado que se cambie el combate y finalmente sean Johnny Walker (23-10) y Waldo Cortés-Acosta (17-4) los que se enfrenten en peso pesado. Al ser peso completo, ambos peleadores no tienen la necesidad de realizar un corte de peso severo, de ahí que hayan podido aceptar en corto aviso. Además, será un combate importante para la parte alta de la división, ya que el ganador entrará de lleno en la lucha por ser uno de los próximos contendientes al cinturón. Por un lado, Waldo viene de un 2025 frenético, en el que peleó hasta en cinco ocasiones y acumuló cuatro victorias que le colocaron a las puertas del cinturón. En 2026 también noqueó a Derrick Lewis el pasado enero, pero en sus dos últimas peleas ha caído derrotado ante Alexander Volkov y Curtis Blaydes y ha visto frenadas sus aspiraciones. En el caso de Walker, cabe destacar que decidió subir a peso pesado tras sus altibajos en peso semipesado, donde no logró cumplir con las expectativas que se pusieron sobre su figura cuando irrumpió con fuerza en la UFC. Su debut en la división se tradujo en un brutal K.O. de rodilla ante Mick Parkin en el primer asalto el pasado 6 de octubre, y su intención es seguir en la misma senda para acercarse al título. Poco a poco ha ido saliendo más información acerca de este cambio de planes en la UFC, y el propio Sean Brady ha compartido unos vídeos en los que muestra que ha sido una infección por estafilococo en su rodilla lo que ha provocado que no pueda pelear ante Bonfim. Este tipo de enfermedades se suelen contraer en los gimnasios y pueden llegar a ser muy graves, por lo que han decidido ser precavidos y bajarse de la pelea. La UFC intentó buscar un rival para Bonfim pero no ha sido posible, por lo que han decidido optar por un Plan B que pueda salvar el evento en el APEX. Aún no se sabe si el duelo entre Bonfim y Brady se volverá a agendar para los próximos meses, ya que son dos de los mayores prospectos de las 170 libras y la recuperación por estafilococo no suele ser muy larga, pero todavía no se sabe nada al respecto.
